reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / Scriver's OMMBID
clinicalPearls: Produces prominent somatic disease, including dysostosis multiplex, coarse facies, and organomegaly, while intelligence is characteristically preserved
Caused by deficiency of arylsulfatase B (N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfatase), impairing dermatan sulfate degradation
Dermatan sulfate is the main glycosaminoglycan that accumulates and is excreted, with no heparan sulfate elevation
Corneal clouding, cardiac valve disease, and carpal tunnel syndrome are common
Severity spans a wide spectrum from rapidly progressive infantile disease to slowly progressive attenuated forms
Cervical cord compression from dural thickening and atlantoaxial changes is an important complication
Diagnosis rests on deficient arylsulfatase B activity with isolated urinary dermatan sulfate and ARSB genotyping
reference.pathophysiology: Maroteaux-Lamy syndrome results from biallelic pathogenic variants in ARSB, causing deficiency of arylsulfatase B (also called N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfatase). This enzyme is required for the lysosomal degradation of dermatan sulfate, so its deficiency leads to accumulation of dermatan sulfate within lysosomes of connective tissue, cartilage, bone, cornea, heart valves, and meninges. The resulting multisystem storage produces the characteristic skeletal, ocular, and cardiac disease. Because heparan sulfate metabolism is unaffected and the brain is relatively spared, cognition is typically normal despite severe somatic involvement. Excess dermatan sulfate is excreted in the urine. Inheritance is autosomal recessive, and residual enzyme activity correlates broadly with disease severity.
additionalDifferentials: Mucolipidoses with skeletal and connective tissue features
Other storage disorders with coarse facies and organomegaly
additionalInvestigations: Leucocyte arylsulfatase B enzyme assay with confirmation against another sulfatase to exclude multiple sulfatase deficiency
Quantitative urinary glycosaminoglycan analysis showing isolated dermatan sulfate
Cervical spine imaging for atlantoaxial instability and dural thickening
Slit-lamp examination and audiology for ocular and hearing involvement
redFlags: Cervical cord compression from dural thickening or atlantoaxial instability
Progressive cardiac valve dysfunction and heart failure
reference.prognosis: Outlook varies widely with disease severity; rapidly progressive forms cause early cardiorespiratory and skeletal complications, while attenuated forms allow survival into adulthood. Enzyme replacement therapy improves endurance and some somatic manifestations but does not reverse established skeletal or corneal disease.
pitfalls: Confusing the enzyme deficiency with multiple sulfatase deficiency without confirmatory testing
Failing to evaluate the cervical spine before anaesthesia
Assuming preserved intellect excludes a mucopolysaccharidosis
Overlooking silent valvular heart disease requiring surveillance
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Enzyme replacement therapy with recombinant arylsulfatase B (galsulfase) as the disease-specific mainstay to improve endurance and reduce dermatan sulfate storage
Consider haematopoietic stem cell transplantation in selected severe early-onset cases
Surveillance echocardiography for valvular heart disease, with valve repair or replacement when indicated
Cervical spine imaging and monitoring for atlantoaxial instability and dural thickening, with decompression or stabilisation surgery for cervical cord compression
Manage somatic complications: carpal tunnel release, hip and other orthopaedic surgery, corneal grafting for visual loss, and hearing aids or grommets for hearing loss
Careful peri-operative airway assessment given difficult intubation and cervical instability
Autosomal recessive: offer genetic counselling and family screening
Coordinate multidisciplinary metabolic, cardiac, orthopaedic, ophthalmic and ENT care
